name: Eyepullmaxxing

lead: Eyepullmaxxing is the community term for a routine in which people pull the outer corners of their eyes upward or outward, by hand or tape, to try to make the eyes look more upturned, which is associated with the 'hunter eyes' look.
Proponents hope it improves the tilt of the eyes. No published study has tested it.

paras: People pull the outer corner of the eye in short sessions, sometimes with tape, and compare photos over time. Tutorials circulate on video and forum platforms.
The skin around the eyes is thin. Repeated pulling can stretch or irritate it, and tape adhesives can cause skin reactions.

chain: Proponents hope for a more upturned eye shape
angle.text: The routine is used in the hope of a more upturned outer eye corner and the hunter-eyes look; it is a non-surgical alternative to canthoplasty.

lead: Eyepullmaxxing is a looksmaxxing term for pulling the outer eye corners, usually upward and outward, to try to change the look of the eyes. It is tied to the idea of hunter eyes, a look with a positive canthal tilt in which the outer corner sits higher than the inner.

The canthus is the corner where the upper and lower lids meet, and the line between the two canthi defines the top of the midface [1]. Surgical canthoplasty reshapes the canthi for cosmetic or functional reasons [1]. Eyepullmaxxing is a non-surgical attempt at the same goal.
No published studies have tested manual or taped eye pulling as a way to change canthal tilt, and its claimed results come from personal reports.

paras: The routine targets the lateral canthus, the outer corner of the eye [1]. Hunter eyes refers to a positive canthal tilt with a lower upper-eyelid exposure; the term comes from looksmaxxing culture.
Canthoplasty is the medical procedure that reshapes the medial or lateral canthus for cosmetic or functional reasons [1].
